## `pm:blocked` — `Blocked-by: #18823`. Measured, not assumed.

This card cannot be dispatched while PR #18867 is open, and the reason is a **hard file serial**, not a judgement call:

| | |
|---|---|
| PR #18867's complete file list | **`.changeset/18677-validate-per-package-authoring-pass.md`** — one file, nothing else |
| this card's named files | `.changeset/18677-validate-per-package-authoring-pass.md`, `.changeset/18778-lint-per-package-authoring-pass.md`, `.changeset/18779-per-package-dedup-positional-key.md` |

⇒ the overlap is exact on `18677-…`. Same **file** is a hard serial in this lane (same *package* is exempt). ⛔ Dispatching this card now would put two branches on one changeset file, and the loser silently drops the other's correction.

### ⚠️ The coupling is not just mechanical — it is the same file's same defect class

PR #18867 is parked on a `Maintainer-action:` (`5724913518`), and its content must be **re-derived** before it can land: #18878 falsified its `After: both report 4`. This card then records a **second** defect in that same changeset — a sentence the CLI source now explicitly forbids restating, attributed to `compile.ts`, which no longer says it.

⭐ ⇒ they are one piece of work on one file, and fixing either alone leaves the file wrong. Whoever unparks #18823 should take both together.

### ⏳ What this park now costs, recorded once and ⛔ not re-asked

This card carries a **hard deadline of its own**: 「下次发版即固化」 — the two changesets are **pending and unreleased**, so the next release writes the retired sentence into the CHANGELOG permanently, where it stops being a pending correction and becomes published history.

⛔ That is **not** an argument for dispatching around the park, and ⛔ not a reason to re-ask the maintainer. It is recorded so the cost of the park is visible when it is next looked at, rather than discovered after a release.

### ⛔ Why this was not split to dispatch the other two files

Two of the three files (`18778-…`, `18779-…`) are free, so a fenced dispatch was possible. It was declined: the three assertions are **one claim in three places**, and landing two of them leaves the card open, the file set half-corrected, and a future reader unable to tell which of the three was deliberate. ⇒ a half-corrected claim is worse than an uncorrected one, because it looks settled.

## `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue` — the file serial is released, and the card's full scope **survives** it

<sub>`domain:cli` execution PM seat #6024 · session `session_01QCdUBjM47SxioST9z5Zwdf` · read 2026-09-21T07:09Z · every row below measured on `origin/main` `eec56c37df`, ⛔ nothing from the closing event</sub>

### ① The blocker's DELIVERY is on `origin/main`, ⛔ not merely closed

`5750251400` named one condition: *"This card cannot be dispatched while PR #18867 is open"* — a hard file serial on `.changeset/18677-validate-per-package-authoring-pass.md`.

PR #18867 is **merged**; card #18823 is closed `completed`. Delivery verified by content, ⛔ not by the merge event:

```
git log origin/main -- .changeset/18677-validate-per-package-authoring-pass.md
  03008c7e1a  docs(cli): #18769's pending changeset declares the `os validate --strict`
              narrowing an at-tier review exhibited (#18867)
  095c7f60ae  fix(cli): `os validate` runs the per-package author-time rule pass … (#18769)
```

⇒ `03008c7e1a` is the #18867 delivery, and it is the file's tip. The serial is released.

### ② ⭐ The card's own defect is **untouched** by that landing — measured, ⛔ not assumed

`5750251400` said the two were *"one piece of work on one file"* and that whoever unparked #18823 should take both. They were **not** taken together. All three named files are still present and unreleased, and the sentence this card is about is still in all three — so each hit was **opened**, because a raw count of 3 is exactly what the card predicts and ⛔ not what it asks for:

| file:line on `origin/main` | what the hit actually is | this card's scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `18677-…md:7` | *"**By `compile.ts`' own description** the survivors of that second pass are «exactly the set the union could not see»"* | ✅ **assertion — still to fix** |
| `18778-…md:11` | *"every finding that pass produces — «exactly the set the union could not see», **in the build command's own words**"* | ✅ **assertion — still to fix** |
| `18779-…md:52` | *"**Also corrected:** the sentence «…», **which was false** for as long as the key was positional"* | ⛔ **legitimate quoted correction — ⛔ do not touch**, exactly as the card's own third-hit section says |

### ③ The contract they contradict is still in force

- `packages/cli/src/utils/artifact-packages.ts:97` 「the key becomes position-insensitive, ⛔ not collision-proof」, `:101` and `:241` 「deliberately narrower than "exactly the set the union could not see"」.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts:458-470` carries the prohibition the card quotes. ⚠️ For whoever takes this: the words are **wrapped across `:468-470`**, so a single-line grep for the card's quoted spelling returns 0 — ⛔ that zero is the instrument, not the tree.

### ④ State

`pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`. Assignee unchanged. ⛔ No re-grading: `priority:p2` and `bug` are triage's and are untouched.

⏳ The card's own 「下次发版即固化」 deadline is **unchanged and still running** — these two changesets are pending, so the next release publishes the retired sentence into `CHANGELOG.md` permanently. Recorded, ⛔ not re-asked.

```text
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — quoted from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --tier --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack .changeset/18677-validate-per-package-authoring-pass.md .changeset/18778-lint-per-package-authoring-pass.md`, run in a detached worktree at `eec56c37df`: "no path-derived mandate … The tier stays the PM's per-card judgment call (floor sonnet · default opus · ceiling fable)." Judged DEFAULT.
Clause-②: no
Labels you may write: none. ⛔ This card needs no label to reach its gates — see "Why no `skip-changeset`" below, which is measured, not assumed. If your own measurement disagrees, ⛔ do not write a label: report it and this seat writes it.
```

### The `Clause-②: no`, declared by this seat with its reason

The diff is **prose in two unreleased `.changeset/*.md` files**. It adds no export, no key, no member, no registration; it moves no accept set in either direction; no code path changes. The sentence being retired is a **description** of a filter, and the filter itself was already corrected by #18779 — this card only stops two entries from restating the retired version as if it were `compile.ts`' own words.

⛔ The declaration is this seat's judgement and it is made here, ⛔ not handed to you. If your reading of the finished diff contradicts it, that is a finding: say so in the report and ⛔ do not change the declaration yourself.

### Why no `skip-changeset` — measured on the adjacent precedent, ⛔ not recalled

PR #18867 (card #18823) edited **exactly one** of these same files, `+16/-1`, landed, and carried labels `documentation, size/s, tooling` — ⛔ **no `skip-changeset`**. The diff touches `.changeset/`, which is what the changeset gate reads. ⇒ your round needs no label to go green. ⚠️ If `Check Changeset` reds anyway, that is a real finding about the gate and ⛔ not a cue to invent a label.

### What to change, and the wording that is already settled

Two assertions, both quoting a source that now **forbids** the sentence:

| file:line on `eec56c37df` | the assertion |
| --- | --- |
| `.changeset/18677-validate-per-package-authoring-pass.md:7` | *"**By `compile.ts`' own description** the survivors of that second pass are «exactly the set the union could not see»"* |
| `.changeset/18778-lint-per-package-authoring-pass.md:11` | *"every finding that pass produces — «exactly the set the union could not see», **in the build command's own words**"* |

⭐ **The correct bound already exists in the tree — ⛔ do not invent a third spelling.** `packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts:457-470` and `packages/cli/src/utils/artifact-packages.ts:236-246` both state it:

> what survives is the set of per-package findings **no union finding already carried under the same rule, `where`, message and non-top-level position**. ⛔ Do not re-inflate that to "exactly the set the union could not see"

⚠️ **Read those two docblocks at the head you branch from before you write a word.** They also say *why* it is narrower (two entries rendering the same `where` still collapse), and an amended changeset that states the bound without that caveat would be the same defect one notch smaller.

### ⭐ The third file: `.changeset/18779-…md` — ⛔ do not touch it, and here is the non-obvious reason

The card already cleared `18779-…md:52` as a legitimate **quoted correction**. There is a second thing in it you will see and may be tempted to fix — at `:55-56` it claims the sentence *"is now stated at the bound the pass can actually hold, **in every file that carried it**"*, and that claim is **false today**, falsified by the two rows above.

⇒ ⭐ **your fix makes it true.** Once both assertions are corrected, `18779`'s completeness claim holds as written, so editing `18779` would be a no-op that costs a third file on the serial. ⛔ Leave it. ⚠️ **Verify this rather than trusting it**: after your edit, re-run the sweep over the whole `.changeset/` population and show that the only surviving hit is `18779`'s quoted correction.

### Measurement this seat expects in the report

- The sweep over **every** `.changeset/*.md`, whitespace-normalised (the sentence wraps across lines), with a **lit control** — the card records that this seat's first attempt printed `0` from a loop that double-prefixed `.changeset/`, while two direct reads each returned 1. ⛔ A zero is not a reading until a control hits.
- ⛔ **Open every hit.** A raw count of 3 is exactly what a correct tree looks like before the fix and 1 after it; the count alone distinguishes nothing.
- The 19 gate commands derived for this surface, run and reported by name.

### ⭐ Refuse this sketch where it is wrong

This order is a sketch and the seat has been wrong eleven times this shift, twice in ways a dev caught. If the settled bound does not fit the sentence either entry is making, if correcting `18677` requires touching the `**BREAKING**` section PR #18867 just added to it, or if the two entries turn out to need *different* corrections rather than one — ⛔ **say so and stop.** A refusal with a measurement behind it is the outcome this seat wants; a compliant patch built on a wrong premise is not.

### ⏳ The clock, unchanged

Both entries are **pending and unreleased**. The next release writes the retired sentence into `packages/cli/CHANGELOG.md` permanently. ⛔ That is context, ⛔ never a licence to skip a measurement.

## Round grade — **ACCEPT** on the diff · ⛔ **order error #12 is this seat's**, the dev caught it · parked on a person's word

<sub>`domain:cli` execution PM seat #6024 · session `session_01QCdUBjM47SxioST9z5Zwdf` · graded 2026-09-21T07:33Z · every reading below re-taken by this seat at source, ⛔ none adopted from the hand-back</sub>

### ⛔ First, this seat's own error — #12, and it is the error-#8 shape again

The claim `5756759699` told the dev, in a section headed *"Why no `skip-changeset` — measured on the adjacent precedent, ⛔ not recalled"*:

> PR #18867 … landed, and carried labels `documentation, size/s, tooling` — ⛔ **no `skip-changeset`**. … ⇒ your round needs no label **to go green**. ⚠️ If `Check Changeset` reds anyway, that is **a real finding about the gate**.

The **instruction** was right and the dev followed it (zero labels written). The **reason** was inverted, and the dev said so instead of accommodating it. Re-measured **by this seat**, ⛔ not taken from the report — PR #18867's merged head `1056c001953497cb83bba50debd6f4784c0d962a`:

```
Check Changeset | completed | failure     (two runs, both on that head)
```

⇒ #18867 **did not go green**. It merged **over** that red. So "no label ⇒ green" was never what the precedent showed, and "a red here is a finding about the gate" was the exact opposite of the truth: this red is the gate **working**.

⭐ The defect is the same one as order error #8: **one field of a precedent was opened (the label set) and a second was inferred from it (the CI outcome) without being opened.** "Read the precedent, don't recall it" is not satisfied by reading *part* of it. The right authority for "write no labels" was never #18867's label set — it is **ruling D on #18375** (maintainer, 2026-09-18T00:00Z), quoted in `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml:735-737`: 「the `skip-changeset` label is never applied to a PR that edits an existing changeset」 — and it is present in that workflow at #18867's own merge commit `03008c7e1a`, so it does not post-date the precedent either.

⛔ This seat takes the dev's option **A** on that question: the correction is to the seat's dispatch text, ⛔ not a card against a gate that is behaving as its own header, its workflow comment and a maintainer ruling all prescribe.

### The diff — ACCEPT

`.changeset/18677-…md` and `.changeset/18778-…md`, prose only, `+7/-4`, between merge base `eec56c37dfc89086658c1659bb2da869dfa08d4f` and head `2babd1876786eb135509df70ab4fc2ee0113a7f3` — the two shas printed rather than inferred from the branch point.
